chapters.beat: The Traveller steps out at dawn, and the year unrolls ahead like a road of thirteen moons.
text: On the first morning of the year, the Traveller woke before the sun and stood at the gate with a lantern, a walking stick, and a road that had not been there the night before.

The road ran out of the dark in a long golden line, over hills the Traveller had never seen, and it was marked — the way old roads are marked — with thirteen pale stones, one for every moon of the year.
"Thirteen moons," said the Traveller. "Twenty-eight days apiece. Three hundred and sixty-four days, and one day left over for standing still and looking back."
A small spark of light came drifting down from the gatepost, the way sparks do when a fire is glad to see you, and it lit on the lantern's rim to warm its hands.
"Well," said the Traveller, "if the road is going to be that long, I had better start at the beginning." And the two of them stepped out together into the first light.
chapters.title: The Gate at First Light
chapters.synopsis: At dawn the Traveller steps out, and the year unrolls ahead — a road of thirteen moons.

hum.note: the Whistle — the road's constant, sounded over the home root

chapters.beat: At the companions' clearing, the Traveller learns that nobody walks the year alone.

episode.label: Episode 2 — the animated telling of this chapter. The written chapter below is its guide card.

text: The road's first turning led into a clearing where the sparks lived — dozens of them, drifting over the grass like slow fireflies, each one a different colour, each one humming a tune of its own.
Some were red as banked coals and quick. Some were blue as deep water and calm. One, the colour of new leaves, kept hiding behind the Traveller's hat and giggling, if a spark can be said to giggle.

An old keeper of the clearing nodded at the spark on the lantern. "That one has been waiting at your gate a long while," the keeper said. "Sparks are born of the day they are found, and no two are ever alike. Yours knows your name already."

The Traveller held out a hand, and the little spark settled on it — warm as a held coal, light as a rumour — and the whole clearing brightened, just a little, the way a room does when a friend comes in.
"Then we walk together," said the Traveller. And the spark, who had been waiting so patiently, shone.
chapters.title: A Friend for the Road
chapters.synopsis: At the companions' clearing, the Traveller learns that nobody walks the year alone.

chapters.beat: The Traveller learns to read the road's milestones: thirteen moons, twenty-eight days each.

episode.label: Episode 3 — the animated telling of this chapter. The written chapter below is its guide card.

text: Beyond the clearing, the road climbed a long hill, and at the top the Traveller stopped and looked back — and understood the road for the first time.

It was laid out like a great wheel in the land. Thirteen pale stones ringed it, near as the Traveller's own gate and far as the horizon, and between every two stones the road ran straight and even: twenty-eight days of walking, no more, no less.
"Every moon the same length," said the Traveller, counting on fingers. "Every week seven days. Nothing ragged, nothing left hanging. A body could set their heart by a road like this."

The little spark flew ahead and lit on the nearest stone, which bore a name and a number, and the Traveller read them by its light and wrote them in a pocket notebook, in a careful hand: where they were, and what day it was, and what the day was for.
Then they walked on into the first moon, and the road began to feel less like a journey and more like a rhythm — the way a song feels once you know the chorus.
chapters.title: The Road of Thirteen Moons
chapters.synopsis: The road's milestones: thirteen moons, twenty-eight days each — and how to read them.

chapters.beat: A door standing in the road opens onto one single day, whole — and the Traveller steps in.

episode.label: Episode 4 — the animated telling of this chapter. The written chapter below is its guide card.

text: One morning deep in the year, the Traveller came to a door standing in the middle of the road, with no wall around it and no house behind it — only a brass ring turning slowly above it, and the whole sky wheeling gently beyond.
"A door to where?" asked the Traveller. The little spark spun once, delighted. "To today," it seemed to say. "All of it. At once."

The Traveller turned the handle and stepped through — and stood inside the day itself. The day lay round about like a small round country: morning at one edge, evening at the other, the hours standing in their places like fence posts, and everything the day held laid out to be seen.

There were the day's own errands, written on a slate by the path. There was the weather, coming over the little hills. There was a quiet corner where the day kept its one clear thought, waiting to be noticed.

"Most days I only ever see the hour I'm standing in," said the Traveller. "I never knew a day had so much room in it." And they walked the whole day through, slowly, before stepping out the far side and back onto the road.
chapters.title: Through the Day Door
chapters.synopsis: A door standing in the road opens onto one single day, whole. The Traveller steps in.

chapters.beat: Inside a walled garden of thirteen beds — one waking at a time — the Traveller learns patience.

episode.label: Episode 5 — the animated telling of this chapter. The written chapter below is its guide card.

text: The road bent at the garden wall, where a gate with a gear for a latch stood open, and inside there were thirteen long beds in rows, with brass corners and lantern light, and rich dark earth in every one.

But only one bed was awake. In it, green things were coming up in the order the season allows. The other twelve slept under their covers of leaves — one for every moon of the year, the gardener said, and each wakes in its own moon and no other.
"You plant what the ground is ready for," said the gardener, "and you plant it in its bed's own moon. Not before. Not after. The year is a garden that walks, if you let it."

The Traveller helped carry water, and stood a while in the quiet, and the little spark drifted over the beds and found — tucked at the foot of the waking one — a single bright seed that nobody had planted, which the gardener said was a gift and to keep it safe.
When they left, the gate clicked shut behind them with its gear-latch, and the Traveller carried the seed in a pocket, wrapped in a leaf, all the rest of the road.
chapters.title: The Garden of Thirteen Beds
chapters.synopsis: A walled garden of thirteen beds, one waking at a time, teaches patience.

chapters.beat: At the storehouse, the Traveller packs scrolls and tools for the long road ahead.

episode.label: Episode 6 — the animated telling of this chapter. The written chapter below is its guide card.

text: Every long road has a storehouse somewhere along it, and this road's stood where the path came down to the river: shelves and shelves of scrolls, maps rolled in tubes, tools oiled and laid in rows, everything kept ready for travellers.
"Take what the road ahead asks for," said the storekeeper. "Not everything. A pack too heavy makes a short road of a long one."
So the Traveller chose carefully: the map of the moons, a small book of the road's own words, one tool for mending, one for measuring starlight — and rolled them all in oilcloth against the rain.
The little spark inspected the pack and approved it, and rode on top the rest of the day like a captain on a ship.
"Now," said the Traveller, shouldering the pack, "we are properly setting out. Everything before this was only leaving."
chapters.title: Packing for the Way
chapters.synopsis: At the storehouse, the Traveller packs scrolls and tools for the long road ahead.

chapters.beat: At a crossroads stands a desk where a Witness writes down the road, exactly as it happens.

episode.label: Episode 7 — the animated telling of this chapter. The written chapter below is its guide card.

text: Where five roads met there stood a desk under a lantern, and at the desk sat the Witness, writing in a great book with a brass clasp.

"What do you write?" asked the Traveller. "The road," said the Witness. "Exactly as it happens. Not as it was wished, not as it was feared. As it happens. It is the whole of my work, and it is enough."

The Traveller told the tale of the road so far — the gate, the clearing, the wheel of moons, the day door, the garden, the storehouse — and the Witness wrote it all down in a clear hand, and read it back, and it was the same tale, only truer for having been kept. When the garden day came round in the reading, the Witness had written only, "He waited by the waking bed," though the Traveller's telling had made a morning's work of carrying water; the Traveller saw the difference, and let it pass.
"A road unwitnessed is only half walked," said the Witness, closing the book. "Yours is kept now. Walk on."

And the Traveller walked on into the next moon, with the little spark riding the lantern, and the road unrolling ahead — and behind them, in the great book at the crossroads, their story so far stood written, where anyone coming after could read how the way went.
chapters.title: The Desk at the Crossroads
chapters.synopsis: At a crossroads stands a desk where a Witness writes the road down, exactly as it happens.

chapters.title: The Signpost Meadow
chapters.beat: Past the crossroads, a meadow of signposts shows the Traveller the short road and the long one.

episode.label: Episode 8 — the animated telling of this chapter. The written chapter below is its guide card.

text: Past the crossroads the road came to a meadow, and the meadow was full of signposts — dozens of them, planted like a young orchard, every one carved with a name and an arrow.

"For the traveller in a hurry," read the nearest, "the whole road in three minutes: the gate, the moons, the spark, the garden." And beneath it, in smaller letters: "For the traveller in earnest, the same road, walked slowly."

The Traveller walked the short way first, the way the signpost taught — and it was a true way, as far as it went. The little spark approved. "A short road that tells the truth about the long one," it seemed to say, "is a kindness."
"And when I come back with more time?" asked the Traveller. Every signpost in the meadow turned, just slightly, the way sunflowers turn — all of them pointing onward, deeper in.
So the Traveller took the short road gratefully, and marked the meadow well, for it is a good thing to know where the beginnings are kept.
chapters.synopsis: A meadow of signposts shows the Traveller the short road and the long one.

chapters.title: The Roundhouse of Engines
chapters.beat: A roundhouse by the road keeps the great systems — each one an engine with its own work.

episode.label: Episode 9 — the animated telling of this chapter. The written chapter below is its guide card.

text: The road passed a roundhouse then, broad and low, with many doors around its curve, and from inside came the sound of great slow machinery, patient as a mill-stream.

Each door had a name over it, and behind each door an engine with its own work: one that kept the calendar's turning, one that kept the record straight, one that carried words from place to place, one that watched the road itself.
"None of them is the road," said the roundhouse keeper, polishing a brass fitting. "Travellers mistake that, sometimes. The engines serve the road. The road serves the walking."
The little spark darted from door to door, reading the names, and came back looking pleased with the order of things.
The Traveller wrote the names in the pocket notebook, in the careful hand, and walked on with the sound of the machinery fading kindly behind.
chapters.synopsis: A roundhouse by the road keeps the great systems — each an engine with its own work.

chapters.title: The Workshop That Tests
chapters.beat: In the Remnant Lab, nothing is believed until it has been tried — the Traveller watches a test.

episode.label: Episode 10 — the animated telling of this chapter. The written chapter below is its guide card.

text: Beyond the roundhouse stood a workshop with its doors wide open and its benches covered in half-built things: instruments, models, questions made out of wire and wood.

"This is the laboratory," said the keeper of the place, not looking up from a delicate adjustment. "Everything on these benches is a question. Some of them will turn out to be answers. Most won't, and that's the work too."

On the longest bench, a claim lay in pieces, being tested joint by joint — what it rested on, what would break it, what it could honestly carry. The Traveller watched a while, and understood that this, too, was a kind of respect: to test a thing hard before asking anyone to stand on it.
The little spark hovered over a small engine that hummed a single clear note, and hummed back, a third higher, and for a moment the whole workshop sounded like a chord.
"Come back when your question is built," said the keeper. "We'll test it together." And the Traveller walked on, thinking of questions as things you build.
chapters.synopsis: In the Remnant Lab, nothing is believed until it has been tried.

chapters.title: The Practice Yard
chapters.beat: A yard beside the road where travellers drill the small daily exercises that keep a walker strong.

episode.label: Episode 11 — the animated telling of this chapter. The written chapter below is its guide card.

text: Next the road widened into a practice yard, worn smooth by feet, where travellers were doing the small exercises of the road — the same few movements, done daily, done properly.

One balanced a cup of water across the yard without spilling, learning attention. One repeated a name until it rang true, learning the weight of words. One simply stood still for the length of a song, learning that stillness is also a practice.
"Nobody becomes a walker by reading about walking," said the yard-keeper, handing the Traveller the cup. "A little, every day, in the open air. That's the whole secret, and it isn't one."
The Traveller carried the cup across without spilling more than a drop, and the little spark drank the drop, and shone.
They walked on with steadier steps than they had arrived with, which is the yard's whole harvest.
chapters.synopsis: A yard beside the road, where travellers drill the small daily exercises that keep a walker strong.

chapters.title: The Picture Lesson
chapters.beat: A lesson taught in pictures: the Traveller learns to see a thing whole before naming its parts.

episode.label: Episode 12 — the animated telling of this chapter. The written chapter below is its guide card.

text: In a quiet room off the practice yard, a teacher was giving a lesson with no words at all — only pictures, shown one at a time, each plainer and truer than the last.
"Some things the ear learns slowly and the eye learns at once," said the teacher at last. "So we teach the eye first, and let the words catch up when they can."

The Traveller sat on the schoolroom bench — too small, knees up like a grasshopper — and watched a shape become a pattern, and a pattern become a meaning, the way clouds become rain: gradually, then all at once.
The little spark, who had no eyes to speak of, understood perfectly, which the teacher said proved the lesson was a good one.
"See it whole," said the teacher, closing the picture book. "Then name the parts. Never the other way round." And the Traveller carried that out of the room like a tool.
chapters.synopsis: A lesson taught in pictures: see a thing whole before naming its parts.

mark.token: the whole seen before its parts

skill.name: See whole before naming
skill.kitMark: the unlabelled drawer, left open by choice

chapters.title: The Second Book
chapters.beat: The Ledger is the road's account book — every entry weighed, dated, and left where anyone may check it.

episode.label: Episode 13 — the animated telling of this chapter. The written chapter below is its guide card.

text: Further on, the road passed a counting-house with tall windows, and inside, on a stand of its own, lay a second great book — not the Witness's book of the road's tale, but the road's account book: the Ledger.

In it, everything the road claimed was entered plainly: what was promised, what was done, what it cost, what changed — each entry dated, each one left open on the desk where any traveller could check it against the world.
"A tale can be beautiful," said the ledger-keeper. "An account must be checkable. The road keeps both books, and never lets them pretend to be each other."
The Traveller turned the pages and found the entries neither flattering nor harsh — just exact, the way a good scale is exact, and kind in the way exactness is kind.

Lower on the page, he found the garden day: "Waited by the waking bed. Carried water. Kept the quiet." The cost stood plainly beside it — one morning — and so did the change: the bed had not waited alone. Beneath the entry, not over it, a correction to the tale had been appended in a clear hand, naming the larger tale told at the crossroads and setting the smaller, truer day beside it. The Traveller read it with heat in his face, for he had let the difference pass and had been quietly ashamed of how little the day seemed to hold; now the account showed him that the little had still been a keeping, and that a day is lost not by being ordinary, but by never being entered at all.
The little spark lit on the book's brass corner and approved, and they walked on, trusting the road a little more for having seen its accounts.
chapters.synopsis: The Ledger is the road's account book — every entry weighed, dated, and open to checking.

chapters.title: The Word-Hoard
chapters.beat: A keeper of words opens the hoard: every name the road uses, kept with its meaning polished bright.

episode.label: Episode 14 — the animated telling of this chapter. The written chapter below is its guide card.

text: The road's next door belonged to the keeper of words, and behind it lay the word-hoard: long shelves of names, each in its own labelled drawer, each with its meaning written out fair.
"Travellers stumble over words more than over stones," said the keeper, pulling a drawer. "So we keep the words the way the garden keeps seeds — sorted, named, and ready to plant."

The Traveller asked after three words the road had used that morning, and the keeper laid them out like tools on a cloth: what each one meant, what it did not mean, and where it had come from, travelling down the years.
One drawer, near the floor, was much larger than the others and bore no label at all. "Some words," the keeper said quietly, "are still being understood. That drawer stays open."

The little spark read every label it could reach, twice, and the Traveller walked on speaking a little more carefully than before — which, the keeper called after them, is the whole point of a glossary.
chapters.synopsis: A keeper of words opens the hoard: every name the road uses, kept with its meaning polished bright.

chapters.title: The High Library
chapters.beat: Above the road stands the high library, where the deep pattern behind the road is studied.

episode.label: Episode 15 — the animated telling of this chapter. The written chapter below is its guide card.

text: From the word-hoard, a stair climbed to the high library, where the road's deep pattern is studied: why thirteen moons, why the day has a door, why a spark is born of a day and never twice the same.

The shelves there held the framework of everything below — the great equation chalked on a board by the window, worked and reworked in a dozen hands; the arguments, kept as carefully as the agreements, for an argument honestly kept is a map of where the thinking has been.
"Downstairs they walk the road," said the librarian. "Up here we ask what the road is. Both are the work. Neither is the whole of it."

The Traveller read until the light changed, and the little spark read over the Traveller's shoulder — if a spark can be said to have a shoulder's worth of reading in it — and neither of them pretended to have finished.
"It goes deeper than one visit," said the librarian, not unkindly, and marked their place with a ribbon. "The library keeps. Come back by any door."
chapters.synopsis: Above the road stands the high library, where the deep pattern behind the road is studied.

chapters.title: The Registry Stall
chapters.beat: At the registry stall, the road's made things are entered in the book and offered to travellers.

episode.label: Episode 16 — the animated telling of this chapter. The written chapter below is its guide card.

text: Where the road came down toward the river again there stood a stall with a striped awning, and on its counter a registry book, and behind the counter the things the road's makers had made: copperwork, stone, bound pages, small bright instruments.
Every made thing was entered in the registry before it was offered — what it was, who made it, what it was for — for the stall-keeper held that a thing you can trace is a thing you can trust.
"Makers make," said the stall-keeper, wrapping a copper spiral in cloth for a traveller ahead in the queue. "The registry remembers. The stall just introduces them."

The Traveller turned the registry's pages and found the entries plain and complete, and the little spark examined a quartz point on the counter and lit it from inside, just for a moment, the way sunlight does.

Then the Traveller opened his pocket notebook at the end of the counter and made a fair copy of the road so far — its names and numbers and days, written again in his neatest hand. It cost him the rest of the morning. When the copy was done, he entered it in the registry himself: "A road kept by its walker, made from the days as they were witnessed." The stall-keeper laid it among the made things, for nothing in the registry could be traced more plainly to the hands that made it.
They bought nothing that day, having miles still to go — but the Traveller wrote the stall's place in the notebook, for some roads you walk twice: once to see, and once to carry home.
chapters.synopsis: At the registry stall, the road's made things are entered in the book and offered to travellers.

chapters.title: The Atlas Room
chapters.beat: In the Atlas room, the whole work lies open at once — every region of the record on one long table.

episode.label: Episode 17 — the animated telling of this chapter. The written chapter below is its guide card.

text: The last room of that stretch of road was the Atlas room, and it was less a room than a table the size of a room: the whole work laid out on it at once, region by region, the way a country lies on a mapmaker's table.

Here was the calendar country, and the theory highlands, and the long shore of the record, and the small bright settlements of the practices — all of it visible together, so a traveller could see not only where a thing was, but what it stood next to, and what it was far from.
"The road you walk one day at a time," said the atlas-keeper. "The Atlas is the same road, seen the way the year sees it: all at once. A traveller needs both views, and must never confuse them."

The Traveller leaned on the table's edge a long while, finding the morning's walk drawn small and true, and the little spark flew the length of the table and back, quick as a rumour, and reported the far end worth the walking.
"Then we walk," said the Traveller, rolling the pocket notebook tight. And the road, which had been waiting politely outside the door the whole time, unrolled ahead into the next moon.
chapters.synopsis: In the Atlas room, the whole work lies open at once on one long table.

note: One continuous story, told a piece at a time across the whole site: the home page opens it, and every page carries the chapter that belongs to that page's own subject, so travelling the site reads the story in the order you walk. It is plainly a story — a traveller's tale told alongside the record, never blended into it. It makes no claims, cites no evidence, and never speaks as Aaron. On Scripture and Evidence surfaces a chapter, if one belongs there at all, travels as plain words only — no cartoon. The story is a living text: it is edited and added to a little at a time as the site grows, and its growth is noted in the growth record like any other growth.

series.note: Series One: the trunk. Seventeen chapters fitted across the site; sixteen carry their animated episode on their own page, and the first chapter's film opens the story on the home page (see openingFilm). Episodes are told apart by name, land, Moon and token — never by number.

series.name: The Living Circuit

The series of the author's own device works — the T-7 resonance conduit, the QRI-16, the Earth's instruments, the Lattice and the Ladder of Scales — animated under the standing laws of those works: refine, never create; the operator completes the circuit; coherence is shown, never printed; no harm at any gate. Five episodes planned; none filmed, no scripts written yet.
